summary: The note surveys ten nature-based learning initiatives at schools, from outdoor classrooms and school gardens to citizen science, survival skills, arts, debate, technology and recycling. Each initiative is tied to a specific school, educator and start date. The overall goal is to bring outdoor and environmental education into daily learning and build environmentally aware students.
one_line: Ten school programs show how nature-based learning is integrated into curricula, from Forest Fridays to gardens, citizen science, and recycling initiatives.
key_facts: Greenfield School District introduced "Forest Fridays" in September 2023, led by Principal Melissa Benson, holding classes outdoors every Friday weather permitting.
Forest Fridays span multiple subjects: math classes measure tree growth rates and English classes write nature-inspired poetry.
East Valley High School, guided by educator James Thompson, launched a school garden and small-scale farming project in October 2023, where students run a mini farmers' market.

Lincoln Middle School made citizen science a cornerstone activity as of 2023, coordinated by science teacher Sarah Kim, with students collecting data on local wildlife, weather patterns, or plant phenology.

Riverside Academy added wilderness survival skills courses to its Physical Education curriculum in Spring 2024, led by Kyle Rodriguez, covering shelter building, edible plant identification and basic orientation.
Hawthorne Elementary's art program, introduced by Laura Garcia in fall 2023, includes nature photography and workshops on making artwork from natural materials.
Marcus Johnson of Coastal Middle School has directed outdoor theater performances since 2024, held in forests or meadows to teach audiences about environmental issues.
Greenview Secondary's debate team, led by coach Anita Das and established in January 2024, focuses on environmental issues.
Omar Chen began geocaching and GPS mapping projects at Tech Valley High School in September 2024.
City View Elementary School runs quarterly nature retreats organized by Emily Torres, with field trips to forests, wetlands, or coastal areas guided by local experts or park rangers.

Belmont High School, assisted by teacher Ryan Peterson, instituted a mandatory recycling initiative in 2023, including student waste audits and proposals to reduce the school community's carbon footprint.
The note cites benefits of outdoor education including improved physical health, mental wellbeing, and deeper understanding of ecological principles.
